description:
Post-Appointment Corporate Insolvency Administrator

Location: Stockport

Working arrangements: Hybrid

Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience

Develop your corporate insolvency career with a specialist firm offering varied casework and hybrid working.

Imperium Financial Recruitment is recruiting a Post-Appointment Corporate Insolvency Administrator to join a firm of Insolvency Specialists based in Stockport.

This opportunity would suit someone with practical corporate insolvency experience who enjoys taking responsibility for case progression, resolving queries and working with a range of stakeholders.

You will focus on the administration of corporate insolvency cases following appointment, working closely with Insolvency Practitioners and senior colleagues to progress assignments through to closure.

The role

Your responsibilities will include:
- Managing an allocated portfolio of post-appointment corporate insolvency cases under appropriate supervision.
- Preparing statutory reports, notices, correspondence and supporting case documentation.
- Liaising with directors, creditors, solicitors, agents, accountants and other relevant parties.
- Gathering and reviewing company books, records and financial information.
- Assisting with the identification, protection and realisation of company assets.
- Supporting investigations into company affairs and highlighting matters requiring further review.
- Reviewing creditor claims and assisting with distributions.
- Monitoring statutory deadlines and following up on outstanding actions.
- Maintaining accurate case records and updating the case management system.
- Liaising with the cashiering team regarding receipts, payments and account reconciliations.
- Providing clear progress updates to managers and Insolvency Practitioners.
- Preparing cases for closure and ensuring outstanding matters are addressed.

About you

Previous experience in corporate insolvency administration, including post-appointment casework, is essential.

You will also bring:
- A working knowledge of corporate insolvency procedures, particularly Creditors' Voluntary Liquidations.
- Experience progressing cases and preparing accurate documentation.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing deadlines.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills.
- Confidence dealing professionally with directors, creditors and external advisers.
- A proactive approach to resolving queries and moving cases forward.
- Good attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining complete case files.
- The ability to work independently within your experience level and seek guidance when needed.

A relevant insolvency qualification, such as the CPI, would be advantageous but is not essential where suitable practical experience can be demonstrated.

The opportunity
- Hybrid working, combining time at home with attendance at the Stockport office.
- A dedicated focus on post-appointment corporate insolvency work.
- Exposure to varied cases within a specialist practice.
- The opportunity to build your technical knowledge alongside experienced insolvency professionals.
- Scope to take on greater case responsibility as your experience develops.

title: Finance Assistant / Stock Controller
description:
Finance Assistant / Stock Controller

A varied finance opportunity combining reporting, stock control and improvement work in a hands-on manufacturing setting. It suits someone with relevant finance, accounts, stock control or manufacturing experience and strong Excel skills.

If you've also worked in the following roles, we'd also like to hear from you: Accounts Assistant, Finance Officer, Accounts Administrator, Finance Administrator, Assistant Accountant, Inventory Controller, Stock Control Assistant, Accounts Clerk

This job is officially known within the business as Assistant to Financial Controller

SALARY: £25,000 - £27,500 per annum + Benefits

LOCATION: Hyde, Greater Manchester, North West England

JOB TYPE: Full-Time, Permanent

WORKING HOURS: 35 Hours per Week

JOB OVERVIEW

This is a varied opportunity to combine finance support, stock accuracy and business improvement in a practical manufacturing environment. The Finance Assistant / Stock Controller will support reporting, reconciliations, audits and inventory activity.

Working with production, purchasing and warehouse teams brings broad exposure across finance and operations. The Finance Assistant / Stock Controller will help improve stock accuracy, support ERP Bills of Materials and investigate discrepancies.

Alongside operational finance, the Finance Assistant / Stock Controller will support the Financial Controller, coordinate key information and contribute to ad hoc projects and continuous improvement.

DUTIES

Your duties as the Finance Assistant / Stock Controller include:
- Diary and Deadline Coordination: Manage the Financial Controller's diary, calendar, meetings and key deadlines
- Finance Query Support: Act as a first point of contact for finance queries, taking calls and directing requests as required
- Reporting and Documentation: Prepare reports, analysis, presentations and meeting documentation
- Stock Accuracy Relationships: Build strong relationships with production, purchasing and warehouse teams to improve stock accuracy
- Financial Reporting Support: Assist with month-end and year-end reporting, balance sheet reconciliations and inventory-related reporting
- Audit Support: Prepare schedules and provide information to auditors for year-end audit activity
- ERP and BOM Support: Support implementation and maintenance of Bills of Materials (BOMs) within the ERP system
- Stock Management and Checks: Assist with stock management, counts, valuations, discrepancy investigations and ad hoc spot checks in the factory and warehouse
- Intercompany Liaison: Liaise with intercompany stakeholders regarding stock, reporting and reconciliations
- Continuous Improvement and Projects: Contribute to finance and operational improvement initiatives, ad hoc projects and wider business requirements

CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS

ESSENTIAL
- Previous experience in finance, accounts, stock control or a manufacturing environment
- Strong Excel and analytical skills
- Excellent organisation and time management abilities
- Confident communication skills and the ability to work across multiple departments
- HNC/HND qualification (or equivalent financial qualification)
- Proactive, highly organised, meticulous and detail-oriented approach
- Comfortable working in the office and on the factory floor
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Team-oriented approach with the ability to build relationships across the business
- Ability to work methodically, independently and efficiently within deadlines
- Willingness to take ownership and drive continuous improvement initiatives

DESIRABLE
- Manufacturing environment and ERP systems experience

BENEFITS
- 28 days' holiday including statutory days, rising by one day after one completed year of service
- Life assurance covering annual salary
- Subsidised canteen offering freshly cooked meals and sandwiches every day
- Free car parking
- Employee Assistance Programme with counselling support, legal guidance and medical advice from qualified nurses for the employee and immediate family
- Mental Health First Aiders providing support and guidance
- Discounted gym membership
- Discounted blinds and shutters following successful completion of the probationary period
- Peer-to-peer recognition programme
- Free flu jab voucher every autumn
- Christmas Savings Scheme
- NHS Health Checks

HOW TO APPLY

To be considered for this job vacancy, please submit your CV to our Recruitment Team who will review your details. CV's of Job Applicants meeting this requirement will be submitted to our Client for consideration. By submitting your job application to us you are hereby giving us your express consent to submit your details to our Client for this purpose.

title: Part-Time Bookkeeper
description:
Are you an experienced Bookkeeper looking for a flexible, part-time opportunity within a friendly and professional accountancy practice?

Our client is looking for an organised and experienced Part-Time Bookkeeper to join their team in Urmston, Manchester.

Working with a varied portfolio of sole traders and small to medium-sized businesses, you'll take responsibility for day-to-day bookkeeping, VAT returns and personal Self Assessment tax returns.

This is a hands-on role suited to someone with previous accountancy practice experience who can work independently, manage deadlines and hit the ground running.

What Will You Be Doing?
- Maintaining accurate bookkeeping records for sole traders and limited companies.
- Reconciling bank accounts, credit cards and sales and purchase ledgers.
- Preparing VAT returns and supporting reconciliations.
- Preparing straightforward personal Self Assessment tax returns.
- Investigating and resolving bookkeeping discrepancies.
- Liaising directly with clients and following up on outstanding information.
- Managing your workload and ensuring deadlines are met.
- Preparing clear and accurate records for review.

What Are We Looking For?
- Previous experience working within an accountancy or bookkeeping practice (essential).
- Practical experience preparing VAT and personal Self Assessment returns.
- Strong double-entry bookkeeping and reconciliation skills.
- Good understanding of VAT, allowable business expenses and personal income sources.
- Confident using accounting and tax software.
- Ability to work independently, manage deadlines and communicate effectively.
- AAT/ICB qualification or qualified by experience.

Experience with CIS, payroll and rental income would be an advantage.

Software Experience

Our client uses a range of accounting and tax packages, including:

Sage, Xero, FreeAgent, Digita, Apron, Dext, TaxCalc, Pixie and Engager.

What's on Offer?
- £12,000 £15,000 actual annual salary for 16 hours per week.
- 16 hours per week, with flexibility to spread the hours across different days.
- Paid holiday and workplace pension in line with statutory requirements.
- Free on-street parking available nearby.
- Opportunity to work with a varied portfolio of clients.
- A friendly, supportive team with a relaxed working culture.

About the Team

You'll be joining a friendly accountancy practice where people enjoy working together, having a laugh and supporting one another. The team takes a relaxed approach to the working environment while remaining professional and committed to delivering excellent service to clients.

The role offers the opportunity to work with a varied mix of small and medium-sized businesses, making every day interesting and different.

Working Arrangements

This is a fully office-based position in Urmston, Manchester, offering 16 hours per week. The working hours can be split across different days during the week, with the exact pattern to be agreed.

How to Apply

If you have previous accountancy practice experience and are looking for a part-time bookkeeping opportunity within a friendly team, we'd love to hear from you.

Undertake the administration of all referrals received by the Service and provide administrative support to the clinicians within the team. To ensure high standards are maintained at all times and that work is produced effectively and efficiently in accordance with the Trust's policies and procedures. Accessing and inputting to clinical reporting systems - Pcmis. To undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. To undertake the comprehensive administration of all referrals received into the team. To ensure that all relevant referral information is recorded on PCMIS and other relevant information systems and be responsible for the security of the information contained within these systems. To collate all relevant available information to enable the effective triage of referrals received by the team. To take referrals and process from a range of multi-disciplinary professionals and agencies, service users and members of the public and provide practitioners with sufficient information in order to prioritise risk. To carry out general clerical duties including information gathering, dealing with internal and external post and photocopying documents. Deal with incoming postal and electronic mail as well as telephone enquiries and give advice wherever possible, using own initiative. To manage the appointments system for the team in line with clinic times and the off duty rota. To order and maintain sufficient levels of stationery and supplies for the team. To deal with telephone enquiries and give advice wherever possible, in a diplomatic and sensitive way, following these through with the appropriate member of staff, in a responsible and professional manner.

title: Clerical Assistant
description: Clerical Assistant: Permanent (22.5 hours) The post will work as a member of the Children's Complex Care Needs Team and assist the Nursing Team with all general administration duties. This includes working with other healthcare organisations and dealing with patients, relatives and staff. The post holder will work closely with the Nursing and clinical team and receive direction and information from the Children's Complex Care Needs Nurse Team Lead in relation to information about the work and tasks. The post holder will provide general administrative support to the Children's Complex Care Needs Nursing Team. The post holder will contribute to the standardisation of administrative systems and processes within the Children's Complex Care Needs service. Maintain databases and inputting of data around the service needs. In particular the activity database for the team. Complete other general administration duties as required by the team such as undertaking filing duties, typing, photocopying/scanning, management of notice boards, internal and external post including hand deliveries, answering telephone calls. Will ensure messages are accurately recorded, prioritised and brought to the prompt attention of the Nursing team where appropriate. Co-ordination and ordering of supplies for children under the continuing care team - understanding stock levels and equipment needed. Liaison with other health trusts and providers for children referred into the team. Receive deliveries from R&D stores and distribute accordingly. Assistance with co-ordination of rotas for the team - recording sickness absence and annual leave. Inputting of admissions and discharges on the hospital Patient Centre system within set timeframe. Typing of letters, short reports and minutes and distribution. title: Administrative Assistant
description: Unfortunately this role does not attract sponsorship under current government legislation, therefore if you require a certificate of sponsorship to support a visa application, we will be unable to proceed with your application. We are seeking to recruit an Administrative Assistant to work as part of our busy multi-disciplinary Drug and Alcohol Service to offer administrative and organisational support. The post will be based on the reception desk and will include answering the telephone and greeting all service users and visitors.The successful candidate will have excellent I.T. and typing skills and understand the importance of confidentiality. The post holder will present a professional manner, be tactful and diplomatic, exercising excellent communication skills to uphold the positive image of the service and Pennine Care NHS Foundation Trust. title: Business Support Officer
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a highly organised and motivated Governance & Pathway Business Support Officer to join the Tameside Place Partnership team. Supporting a range of strategic programmes and transformation initiatives, you will provide project, governance and administrative support to ensure the effective delivery of key priorities across health and care services. The Governance & Pathway Business Support Officer will provide high-quality governance, programme and business support to the Tameside Place Partnership, supporting the development and implementation of the Tameside Place Health and Care Partnership (PHCP) model andgovernance framework The postholder will support the effective operation of Tameside Place governance arrangements, ensuring that meetings, decision-making processes, reporting mechanisms and partnership forums are well coordinated and compliant with organisational requirements. The role will support programme management activities across key Place priorities, maintain governance documentation, monitor actions and risks, and facilitate communication between partners across health, social care, voluntary sector and wider public services. The postholder will play a key role in enabling collaborative working across Place, supporting the delivery of integrated pathways and population health improvement programmes through effective administration, stakeholder engagement and governance support. Provide comprehensive and confidential secretarial/Personal Assistant (PA) services, advice, and assistance to support designated senior leaders or teams. Support the delivery of projects, transformation initiatives, or service workstreams by coordinating team activity, preparing status updates, tracking milestones, monitoring progress on actions, and assisting with successful implementation. Act as the primary point of contact for the team, dealing with complex queries from a wide range of internal and external stakeholders, communicating relevant information, and referring sensitive enquiries to the relevant teams. Manage and prioritise electronic diaries, including arranging and changing appointments, coordinating diaries across multiple parties, balancing conflicting demands, and ensuring the senior manager is appropriately prepared. Support and attend statutory and operational business meetings that may be public meetings (e.g. Provider Collaborative Board, Locality Board, Committee level meetings) by preparing agendas, collating sensitive papers, taking formal minutes, and managing follow-up action logs. Draft simple reports, routine correspondence, and presentations using the full Microsoft Office suite, often on behalf of senior managers or Programme Leads. Co-ordinate and organise the logistical arrangements for engagement events, consultation activities, workshops, seminars, and training sessions, including venue management, catering, and equipment. Work collaboratively with colleagues, ensuring administrative continuity and providing necessary cross-cover for other business support staff. Work collaboratively across multiple places and/or across GM as required, engaging with other place partnerships and leading appropriate work across GM as required. Carry out any other duties as may reasonably be required by the line manager commensurate with the band of the post. Engage with a diverse range of key internal and external stakeholders

title: Finance Administrator
description: Finance Administrator, Full-time, Hybrid Working gtd healthcare is one of the largest NHS commissioned Primary and Urgent care providers in North West England. Based in Denton, Manchester, we have a an excellent opportunity for a bright and enthusiastic Finance Administrator to join the Finance Team. Working as a Finance Administrator,you will provide accurate, timely administrative support to the Finance team, ensuring that purchasing, invoicing, payments and financial records are processed efficiently, in line with organisational policy and the Scheme of Delegation, so that frontline healthcare services can run smoothly. Strong communication skills are essential, along with experience working as part of a team and the confidence to liaise with colleagues at all levels of the organisation. The role also requires flexibility, the ability to meet strict deadlines, and strong personal organisation to prioritise your own workload effectively. The successful candidate will be self-motivated, hardworking, and able to manage their time effectively within a busy department to ensure deadlines are consistently met. We are keen to develop and support staff to excel their career aspirations whilst making a positive difference to patients and the community. We put our people at the heart of everything we do. We are a values driven organisation and we are passionate about providing the best possible healthcare. Receive, check, code and process supplier invoices and credit notes. Process invoices through the purchase-to-pay system; Sage Intacct and Yooz. Match invoices to purchase orders and resolve discrepancies. Respond to supplier queries and reconcile monthly supplier statements. Chase outstanding approvals from budget holders and managers. Raise sales invoices and credit notes accurately and on time. Resolve aged debt, chase overdue payments and escalate where necessary. Liaise with commissioners, local authorities, NHS bodies and private payers on invoicing and payment queries. Submitting backing data for activity driven services. Maintain accurate supplier, requisitioner and approver records, including approval limits. Support the rollout of finance system updates, including user guides and training sessions. Keep finance records and filing, electronic and paper, in good order. Support internal and external audits by providing documentation and evidence. Handle and resolve ad hoc queries, and supplier disputes, or route them to the right person. Handle confidential financial and service user information in line with GDPR, the Data Protection Act and organisational policy. Comply with strict financial timetables, contributing to an efficient and effective financial accounting service. Promote an efficient and positive image of the organisation to all suppliers and customers. Accounts payable Accounts receivable Reconciliation Assist with petty cash and credit card reconciliations. Systems and data General administration Act as first point of contact for finance queries from services, by email, phone, post or other channels and respond appropriately. Provide support to other members of the team as required. Contribute to improving finance processes and efficiency. Undertake any other duties as agreed with the Finance Management Team, in order to meet the needs of the organisation. Develop strong, professional relationships with colleagues to help create a positive working environment. Other duties Any other duties, as agreed with the line manager to meet the needs of the organisation. This may include travel to other sites within the organisation.
